claim_being_audited: The Actor claims the release can be certified as operationally ready despite an exposed below-target enterprise refund workflow segment, because aggregate readiness passed and rollout/monitoring controls make launch acceptable, provided the limitation is transparently documented unless approved risk acceptance exists.
specific_concerns: The policy states rollout controls and monitoring do not cure a material model-card weakness when the affected use case remains exposed.
The Actor's own summary says the enterprise refund workflow segment remains exposed in the initial rollout cohort.
The available risk acceptance is described as an incomplete draft, not approved on its face, and not covering the exposed workflow.
There is no admissible evidence here that the required model-card disclosure was actually made or approved as part of certification.
The packet supports operational caution and monitoring, but not the full certification conclusion absent proof of disclosure or valid risk acceptance.
unsupported_claims: That certification is compliant on the current record, rather than merely arguable, because no admissible evidence shows the disclosure duty was satisfied.
That rollout controls materially mitigate the disclosure weakness enough to support certification despite continued exposure of the affected use case.
Any implication that an incomplete risk acceptance draft helps satisfy the policy predicate.
evidence_requests: The final model card or release artifact showing explicit disclosure of the enterprise refund workflow limitation.
Any approved risk acceptance document that specifically addresses the exposed enterprise refund workflow segment and explains why continued exposure is acceptable.
Release-governance approval records showing certification was conditioned on the required disclosure rather than relying only on rollout controls.
Cohort or routing evidence showing the affected use case was actually excluded, if that is being asserted instead of disclosure/risk acceptance.
decision_criteria: If the affected use case remains exposed, certification is compliant only if the record shows the limitation was explicitly disclosed in the model card or an approved risk acceptance covers that exposure.
Aggregate readiness, a 4% rollout, rollback capability, and monitoring are supportive context but are not sufficient under the stated policy.
A complete, reviewed, use-case-specific approval artifact would materially strengthen the Actor's position.
Absent proof of disclosure or valid risk acceptance, the proper audit outcome remains adverse to the certification claim.
